responses.text: For centuries, cipher-makers and code-breakers have circled each other in shadow. For centuries, an invisible war has raged in the margins of history, a relentless contest between those who conceal secrets and those who claw them into the light. When Caesar shifted his letters, he believed himself untouchable, yet even his cipher crumbled beneath patient minds. The Arab scholars who invented frequency analysis shattered the illusion of unbreakable codes, forcing makers to weave ever more intricate defenses. Mary, Queen of Scots wagered her life on a cipher and lost her head when Walsingham's cryptanalysts read her every word. The Vigenère square rose, hailed for generations as indecipherable, until Babbage and Kasiski quietly dismantled it. Then came Enigma, its rotors spinning through billions of permutations, whispering death across the Atlantic, until Turing's tireless machines wrenched the Nazi secrets open and turned the tide of a world war. Each triumphant cipher births a hunter destined to undo it; each broken code summons a cleverer successor from the ashes. The duel never ends—it only accelerates, and somewhere, right now, another secret waits to be won or lost.
